- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent 10-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10% below recent peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in that window.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5–10% from recent peak), model often holds or overestimates; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33 or 0.67–1.00), model often overfits recent trends; use 3–5 day moving average of history as baseline for correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of forecast, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 10–20 days.
